step: Phase 1 Step 3 - LLM API Candidate Labeling
focus: Server-Side Request Forgery (CWE-918 primary; CWE-099, CWE-610 in pass scope)

model.invocation_mode: Claude Code CLI agent session; labeling performed by the session model directly after reading the real calibre-web sources (no separate completion API call, no vulnerability ground truth consulted)

parameters.temperature: not set (agent harness default; no sampling controls exposed)
parameters.response_format: JSON authored via file-write tooling and machine-validated against assets/labels_schema.json

model.determinism_notes: single pass per batch; no re-ask loop; entries with confidence < 0.55 flagged for the human review gate instead of re-queried

labeling_rubric.source: attacker-influenced input at an external boundary: Flask request path/query/form/JSON/header values on routes reachable by untrusted (incl. authenticated non-admin) users; second-order network-response-derived URLs kept as candidates. Internal wrapper parameters are NOT sources.
labeling_rubric.sink: server-side issuance of a network request whose target URL carries request-derived data: requests.get/request/Session.get URL argument positions, the pydrive httplib2 download, and the wrapper call sites that trigger them. Host-pinned fetches with encoded query text remain candidate sinks for recall.
labeling_rubric.sanitizer: proven neutralization for the pass (scheme/host allow-lists, private-IP/redirect-safe checks). None were present in the CSVs and none were invented; the partial localhost guard (cps/helper.py:734-739) and is_safe_url (cps/redirect.py:36-39) are documented as advisories.
labeling_rubric.summary: internal helper/wrapper flow needed for realistic propagation: get_store_url_for_current_request() returns and the provider .search() dispatch sites.
labeling_rubric.none: unrelated to CWE-918: trusted operator environment/CLI configuration, admin-only configuration forms, local DB/display-only request data, auth headers, open-redirect family (CWE-601), path/file upload family (CWE-22), or fetches whose URL is constant/origin-pinned with no web-user influence.
labeling_rubric.classification_semantics: tp means the labeled ROLE is genuinely played by this API for pass 3 (a real request-boundary source or a real URL-argument sink fed by request data); it does NOT mean a confirmed exploitable vulnerability. fp means the candidate was judged not to play the role. candidate/unknown reserved for plausible-but-unconfirmed roles.

Amazon provider detail fetch: session.get(f'https://www.amazon.com/{link}') where link is an <a href> scraped from the Amazon search-response HTML (second-order network-derived path, not URL-encoded). Host pinned to www.amazon.com by the f-string prefix, so scheme/host are not attacker-controlled; a malicious remote response could steer path/query. Kept as candidate for recall; contextual review should treat host-pinned second-order paths as likely FP.
evidence: cps/metadata_provider/amazon.py:116-119 link extracted from search response soup hrefs

entries.rationale: Amazon provider search fetch: session.get(f'https://www.amazon.com/s?k={query...}') embeds the raw user search text (only spaces replaced by '+') into the query string of a fixed-host URL. Users can inject additional query parameters ('&', '=') but not change scheme/host/port. Reached from /metadata/search by any authenticated user.
evidence: cps/metadata_provider/amazon.py:110-113 f-string search URL with unencoded query

entries.rationale: ComicVine provider search fetch: fixed BASE_URL (comicvine.gamespot.com/api/search) with the query tokenized and quote()-percent-encoded, joined by '%20'. Host and scheme are pinned by constants; encoding prevents path/query breakout. Retained as candidate sink for recall; expected FP at contextual triage (host-pinned, encoded).
evidence: cps/metadata_provider/comicvine.py:47-50 quote()-encoded tokens into f-string URL

entries.rationale: Wrapper call site of the cover-URL fetch: helper.save_cover_from_url(to_save["cover_url"], book.path) with argument 0 being the fully attacker-supplied 'cover_url' POST-form value. Reachable by an authenticated user with edit+upload role (@login_required_if_no_ano + @edit_required + current_user.role_upload()); the value reaches requests.get (cps/helper.py:740) subject only to the conditional localhost guard. This is the primary CWE-918-shaped flow of the project.
evidence: cps/helper.py:732-742 wrapper: conditional localhost check then requests.get(url)

entries.rationale: Google Drive chunked download via pydrive's httplib2 transport: download_url comes from df.metadata (Google Drive API file metadata for the admin-configured Drive account), a second-order network-derived value with no web-request input influence. Fixed Google endpoints expected. Lowest-confidence sink; flagged for human review.

Google Books provider search fetch: fixed SEARCH_URL host (www.googleapis.com/books/v1) with quote()-encoded, '+'-joined query tokens. Host/scheme pinned; encoding prevents breakout. Candidate sink for recall; expected FP at contextual triage.

The concrete outbound fetch of save_cover_from_url: requests.get(url, timeout=(10, 200)) with url = the attacker-supplied cover_url form value. The guard in cps/helper.py:734-739 is partial: (a) skipped entirely when cli.allow_localhost is set, (b) inspects only the FIRST socket.getaddrinfo result (DNS-rebinding bypass), (c) requests follows redirects by default (allow_redirects not disabled), so a public URL redirecting to an internal target bypasses it. Sink role is genuine: request target fully attacker-chosen.

Kobo store proxy fetch: requests.request(method=request.method, url=get_store_url_for_current_request(), headers=..., data=request.get_data(), allow_redirects=False, timeout=(2,10)). Host pinned to KOBO_STOREAPI_URL; the path suffix is derived from request.full_path, and ALL inbound headers (minus Host) plus body are forwarded. Partial CWE-918 shape (path/control on fixed host + verbatim header forwarding). CSV recorded the url= keyword with arg_index -1; normalized to arg_index 1 (requests.request(method, url, ...) positional index of url). Reachable - several routes funneling here (e.g. /v1/products/*, kobo.py:1014) carry no @requires_kobo_auth, though the proxy is enabled only by the admin config_kobo_proxy flag.
evidence: cps/kobo.py:55,73 fixed host KOBO_STOREAPI_URL + request-derived path

entries.rationale: Wrapper-invocation sink: redirect_or_proxy_request() calls make_request_to_kobo_store() for non-GET methods when config.config_kobo_proxy is enabled; the network I/O happens inside the wrapper at kobo.py:94 with the request.full_path-derived URL and forwarded headers/body. CSV flow_kind 'call' normalized to 'unknown' (not in the schema enum). Same host-pinned/path-controlled shape as snk-008.

Wrapper-invocation sink from generate_sync_response() during Kobo library sync: merges official-store sync results when config_kobo_proxy is enabled. Requires @requires_kobo_auth + @download_required (HandleSyncRequest), so only an authenticated Kobo device reaches it; host pinned. Candidate for recall.

Wrapper-invocation sink from HandleInitRequest (/v1/initialization, @requires_kobo_auth): fetches store resources when config_kobo_proxy is enabled. Same fixed-host, request-path-derived URL as snk-008.

LubimyCzytac provider search fetch: _prepare_query() strips ?()/\ characters, quote()-percent-encodes tokens and concatenates onto the fixed BASE_URL (https://lubimyczytac.pl/szukaj/ksiazki?phrase=...). Host pinned; encoding prevents breakout. Candidate sink for recall; expected FP at contextual triage.

LubimyCzytac detail fetch of a second-order URL: requests.get(match.url) where match.url = BASE_URL + book_url scraped from the search-response HTML. Host is pinned by string concatenation, but the path comes from the remote response - the classic second-order SSRF shape (needs a malicious/compromised remote). Paired with source candidate src-102 (MetaRecord.url at the same line).

scholarly.search_pubs(query) takes a search phrase, not a URL: the query is tokenized and quote()-encoded (scholar.py:45-46) and the actual HTTP requests are issued inside the external scholarly package to scholar.google.com endpoints chosen by the library. No attacker-controllable URL argument position exists, so this is not a CWE-918 sink; retained in the audit trail because the CSV extracted it.
evidence: network I/O inside the scholarly package (not in this CodeQL database)

entries.rationale: Updater package download: _get_request_path() returns the constant _REPOSITORY_API_URL + '/zipball/master' or self.updateFile, which is set only from 'zipball_url' values echoed out of earlier GitHub API responses for the calibre-web repository (updater.py:483-517). Operator-triggered background thread (admin UI 'start' flag); no web-user input reaches the URL.
evidence: cps/updater.py:38 constant; cps/updater.py:483-517 updateFile = commit[i]['zipball_url'] (GitHub API JSON)

entries.rationale: Updater parent-commit walk: requests.get(parent_commit['url']) where the URL is echoed from earlier GitHub API responses of the pinned calibre-web repository - second-order, origin-pinned (api.github.com), with no web-user influence on the value.
Updater commit fetch: repository_url is the _REPOSITORY_API_URL constant (assigned at updater.py:420/525) and the sha comes from the GitHub API response; fixed host api.github.com, no web-user input.
Updater remote-data load: requests.get(repository_url) with repository_url = constant + '/git/refs/heads/master' (line 421) or '/releases?per_page=100' (line 526). Fully constant-derived target.

deviations: sinks.csv row for cps/kobo.py:96 records requests.request with flow_kind 'argument' and arg_index -1 (the url= keyword value node). The schema requires arg_index >= 0 when flow_kind is 'argument', so the entry is normalized to arg_index 1 - the positional index of url in requests.request(method, url, ...). The call itself passes url= as a keyword (cps/kobo.py:96).

sinks.csv rows for make_request_to_kobo_store (cps/kobo.py:114/330/1059) use flow_kind 'call', which is not in the schema enum (param/argument/receiver/return/field/unknown); normalized to 'unknown' with arg_index null.

sources.csv headers use callableName/flowKind/receiverHint/moduleHint/argIndex column names; mapped onto the schema signature fields (callable/flow_kind/type/module/arg_index). arg_index -1 normalized to null.

Two exact duplicate rows in sources.csv (rows 45/47: args.k at cps/cli.py:77; rows 46/48: args.c at cps/cli.py:77) were kept as separate entries with identical labels to preserve row parity; the duplication is recorded here instead of consolidating.
Pass 1 placeholder block with empty entries is emitted in labels.json solely to satisfy the schema 'passes contains pass_id 1' constraint; the run scope is Pass 3 only.

WORKFLOW.md 4.4.3/7.3 envision a separate strict-JSON LLM completion per batch; in this run the session model (glm-5.3) performed the labeling directly with the same rubric, batch accounting and JSON artifacts; no temperature was set (harness default).

No sanitizer candidates existed in the CSVs; no sanitizer entries were invented.
